reviewNote: Our current take for everyday agentic coding. Same-tier order is editorial, not a measured quality gap. Luna and Haiku coverage is still too narrow to rank; empty tiers are intentional.

models.name: Opus 5.5
points: Most accurate in Rails’ Stage 3 agent tasks.
Sonnet 5.5 edges it on AA’s coding index.
models.rationale: S and first for the broadest converging evidence: Anthropic’s coding rows, AA’s Coding Agent Index, Rauch’s Next.js eval, and the most accurate result in Rails’ Stage 3. First is not a universal win; Sonnet 5.5 edges it on AA’s index and Terminal-Bench, and effort and fallbacks matter.

leadCheck.note: Still #1 after GPT-6.1 Sol and Sonnet 5.5 launched.
leadCheck.reason: GPT-6.1 Sol trails Opus 5.5 on AA’s Coding Agent Index (63 at xhigh vs 66 at max), in Rails’ Stage 3 (60.8% vs 65.3%, both xhigh), and in Agent Arena (#5 vs #2); it leads only in Theo’s own Terminal-Bench run in Codex. Sonnet 5.5 leads AA’s Coding Agent Index (68 vs 66) and Terminal-Bench 4.0 (AA 64% vs 60%; Anthropic 70.6% vs 66.4%), but trails in Anthropic’s FrontierCode 1.1 and CursorBench 4.0 rows, Agent Arena (#3 vs #2), AA’s Intelligence Index (56 vs 58), and Epoch’s ECI, at the highest cost per task on AA’s coding index. Neither challenge converges, so the leader holds.

models.name: GPT-6 Astra
points: Frontier terminal and scientific-task results.
AA: terminal parity with Opus 5.5.
Theo: impressive but inconsistent.
models.rationale: S for strong exact-version terminal and scientific-task evidence, tempered by Theo’s reliability warning. No family-name claims or prices establish this placement.

models.name: Fable 5.1
points: Theo’s pick for consistent instruction following.
97% on Rauch’s Next.js eval.
Behind Opus 5.5 in Anthropic’s newer chart.
models.rationale: S for the combination of strong scoped coding results and a credible evaluator’s everyday-use preference. Its placement is not inferred from Fable 5 or a vendor chart alone.

models.name: Sonnet 5.5
points: Tops AA’s coding agent index at 68.
#3 in Agent Arena, behind Opus 5.5.
Heaviest token use AA has measured.
models.rationale: S for converging exact-version coding results: first on AA’s Coding Agent Index, Terminal-Bench leads in both Anthropic’s and AA’s runs, and #3 in Agent Arena. Placed after the tier’s incumbents because it trails Opus 5.5 in Anthropic’s other coding rows, Agent Arena and AA’s Intelligence Index, and costs the most per task on AA’s coding index.

models.name: GPT-6.1 Sol
points: AA coding index: 63, level with GPT-6 Astra.
Rails’ best overall pick: 60.8% at $0.80 a run.
Behind Opus 5.5 on AA’s index and Rails.
models.rationale: S for converging Astra-level coding evidence: AA’s Coding Agent Index (63 vs Astra’s 62), Rails’ Stage 3 (60.8% vs 62.3%), OpenAI’s DeepSWE chart, and Theo’s own Terminal-Bench run. Placed last in S because Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 lead it in the same independent tests. Its much lower cost does not set the tier.

models.name: Opus 5
points: Strong software-engineering results from Epoch.
Capable predecessor to Opus 5.5.
Newer Claude models lead provider terminal evals.
models.rationale: A for supported software-engineering capability with clearer evidence of newer Anthropic models improving on it. Older Epoch evidence is retained as scoped context rather than treated as current leadership.

models.name: GPT-6 Sol
points: AA coding index: 57, up from 55.
97% on Rauch’s Next.js eval.
Some knowledge-work regressions in AA’s tests.
models.rationale: A for modest independent coding gains and a strong scoped Next.js result. The new release is not promoted to S on lower prices or a nearly saturated framework eval alone.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
points: AA coding index: 55 at max effort.
Close to GPT-6 Sol on that index.
Behind frontier models in provider terminal tests.
models.rationale: A for a competitive exact-version coding baseline in AA’s current same-harness comparison. Retained close to its successor; obsolete July index figures are not pooled with September results.

models.name: Grok 4.7
points: AA coding index: 56, up from 47.
94% on Rauch’s Next.js eval.
Theo reports weak frontend work and loops.
models.rationale: B is a cautious everyday-coding recommendation despite strong measured gains: scoped Next.js results and Theo’s detailed reliability complaints limit confidence. AA’s improved score is not concealed or averaged into the anecdote.

models.name: Grok 4.6
points: AA coding index: 47 at xhigh.
Grok 4.7 improves all three coding components.
Theo also flags 4.6’s speed and usability.
models.rationale: B below Grok 4.7 within this tier because the matched-effort coding evidence favors 4.7, while Theo’s complaints do not establish 4.6 as universally preferable.

models.name: GPT-6 Luna
points: AA coding index: 41, down from 43.
OpenAI's own DeepSWE comparison looks promising.
Too little independent coverage to rank.
models.rationale: Unranked: one independent evaluation family plus a provider-reported scoped comparison is too narrow to make a broad everyday-coding recommendation. Lower cost is not evidence of quality.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
points: AA coding index: 43 at max effort.
Ahead of GPT-6 Luna on that index.
One independent source is too thin to rank.
models.rationale: Unranked: exact-version evidence currently comes from a single predecessor comparison. This is insufficient coverage, not a D-tier judgment.

models.name: Haiku 5.5
points: AA Terminal-Bench 4.0: 33%, up from 0%.
Ahead of GPT-6 Luna in AA’s and Anthropic’s tests.
Too little coding evidence to rank.
models.rationale: Unranked: a provider chart and one independent evaluation, neither a coding-agent comparison with ranked models. Built for subagent and high-volume work; this is insufficient coverage, not a D-tier judgment.
